question: why does the walk read as pushing then dragging rather than flowing
method: 800 steps, gait_profile=lab, control_mode=cpg_residual, frozen checkpoint v4_5b_speed_polish_1m, target pushed 5 m ahead each step
reading: The front-left foot carries load only 20 % of the cycle against a 70 % target, and the front-right 59 %. The hind limbs are near their 76.5 % target. So the back end propels on schedule while the front end is off the ground far more than it should be -- which is exactly the push-then-drag rhythm a viewer sees. It is not a rendering artefact and not a tuning failure.
cause: FAILURE_MAP #18, already confirmed: the forelimb has ONE free joint against the hindlimb's TWO, so it cannot set foot height and foot position independently. #17 measured the consequence directly -- the forefoot sits 3.1 mm airborne. This is why 6 M steps of training never beat the hand-written base (#11), and it is one of the two gates that kept the walker at 4/6.
fix_requires: a forelimb with a second free joint -- a body change, not a controller change. The body is 14/14 on static checks and every piece of gait evidence is tied to its hash, so this is not a side effect of any other work.
